image_description: A male mallard duck (drake) standing on a ground covered with dry leaves and dirt. The duck features the characteristic iridescent green head, white neck ring, grey/brown body plumage, and orange webbed feet. It is viewed from a high-angle side profile.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, flat, and yellowish-green in color, matching the description perfectly.
The eye is visible and appears dark/black, consistent with the taxonomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body shape is robust and compact. The feather texture appears dense and layered, typical of waterfowl.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays the classic Mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, and grey/flank feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: One orange leg/foot is clearly visible. It shows the characteristic webbing between toes. The positioning is anatomically correct for a standing duck.
The folded wing structure is visible along the side, showing proper layering of flight feathers and speculum (blue patch).

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is short, and the characteristic upward curl of the central tail feathers is visible at the rear of the duck.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific species identification (Mallard Drake) and rule out hybrid or misclassified bird types.
To verify the structural integrity of the legs and feet, ensuring no fusion or extra limbs, despite the 'limbless' note in instructions, ducks have distinct limbs requiring pose validation.
To check for edge bleeding between the complex feather textures and the leafy background, a common AI artifact area.
To assess general texture consistency and lighting coherence between the subject and the environment.

focus_areas: Boundary sharpness between duck feet and ground leaves
Anatomical correctness of the webbed foot structure
Consistency of the iridescent head sheen
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the transition between the duck's feet and the ground. AI often struggles with the complex occlusion of leaves around webbed feet. Also, verify if the 'curl' of the tail feathers looks physically attached or like a floating artifact.
